title: Days and dates
summary: Sequence days and months and begin recording time.
subject: maths

difficultyRamp.within: Q1 fills a gap before afternoon. Q2 orders parts of the day using icons. Q3 finds tomorrow. Q4 counts days in a week. Q5 orders three days. Q6 names a month from a calendar. Q7 finds a date in October. Q8 orders yesterday, today and tomorrow. Q9 chooses a unit for a short event. Q10 recognises time units.
difficultyRamp.versus: Easy uses pictures for parts of the day, a week strip and a calendar date. Medium uses before and after across week and month boundaries. Hard works backwards from yesterday, moves two months across a year boundary and reads named time records.

questions.explanation: Morning comes before afternoon. Evening comes after afternoon.
questions.hint: Think about when you have breakfast.

questions.prompt: Put the pictures in order, starting with morning.
questions.explanation: Morning comes first. Afternoon, evening and night come after it.

narration.prompt: Put the pictures in order, starting with morning.

questions.hint: Think about when the sun goes down.

questions.prompt: Today is Monday. What day is tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Tomorrow is the next day. Tuesday comes after Monday.

narration.prompt: Today is Monday. What day is tomorrow?

questions.hint: Think about the next day in the week.

questions.prompt: How many days are in one week?
questions.explanation: A full week has seven days, including Saturday and Sunday.

narration.prompt: How many days are in one week?

questions.hint: Count one box for each day.

questions.prompt: Put the days in order, starting with Monday.
questions.explanation: Tuesday comes after Monday. Wednesday comes next.

narration.prompt: Put the days in order, starting with Monday.

questions.prompt: Which month is this calendar for?
questions.explanation: March is the month on the calendar. The numbers show dates in March.

questions.hint: Look at the name above the dates.

questions.prompt: Put yesterday, today and tomorrow in order.

questions.prompt: Pip blinks. What could we use to time it?
questions.explanation: A blink is very quick. We use seconds for short times.
